Fortuna Vera should be all the better for a recent fourth at the Curragh. Racing in better company, the Joseph O'Brien-trained three-year-old stayed on nicely having missed the break. If getting away on terms, she should go close. Love Sonnet is interesting making a quick return after winning at Killarney.

selections.comment: Having made a winning reappearance in the Vintage Crop Stakes at Navan last month, KYPRIOS can book his Royal Ascot ticket here. Unbeaten in his last eights runs, Aidan O'Brien's remarkable stayer has looked better than ever on recent starts. With upwards of 21lb in hand of these rivals, the seven-year-old can maintain his sequence before heading back to defend his Gold Cup crown. Last year's Ballysax winner Dallas Star has plenty to find on ratings but could get closest to the selection. Cork Derby runner-up Satin looks best of the remainder.

selections.comment: The progressive PORSCHE LAD holds leading claims on his stable debut for Charles Byrnes. A winner at Dundalk on his penultimate start, the four-year-old showed that he was capable of being competitive off his revised mark when narrowly denied back at that same venue. Although yet to show any really worthwhile form on grass, the son of Cotai Glory has had very few opportunities to do so. On pedigree, there has to be every chance that he can improve further on decent ground. Narrowly denied when well punted at Dundalk recently, Chopsticks is interesting on debut for John McConnell. Tatum has to enter the equation too.

selections.comment: With the form of his Tipperary second appearing solid, ROCK OF IRELAND can register a first career success. The Alan McIntyre-trained four-year-old shaped with plenty of promise on his previous start when fourth at Cork on his handicap debut. A lightly-raced gelding with more scope for improvement than the majority of these, he will lack for nothing in the saddle with Georgie Benson taking the ride. Royal runner Reaching High is a significant contender for Willie Mullins. Formerly in the care of the now-retired Sir Michael Stoute, the gelding was a winner at Wolverhampton last summer. Burren Song, a previous winner of this race, is another to consider.

However this switch to quicker ground along with the drop in trip could spark significant improvement. He will need it to beat the former who is fancied to shoulder a penalty after an easy win from the front last time where he jumped much better. His trio of bumper wins promises much more to come.

selections.comment: A tight contest where none of the field can be ruled out. It is veteran FLIC ON VOYOU who appeals most as he has been thriving this year since returning from a break. He was badly hampered by a loose horse last time but travelled strongly and did as well to finish as close as he did. That race has thrown up winners and he ought to go close off an unchanged mark. Sainte Doctor has proven hugely progressive this year winning 3 times before being left poorly placed in a better race last time. The drop in trip combined with the long home straight should suit and he rates the biggest danger along with Malaita who was behind him last time but did travel strongly before her stamina gave way.

That looks strong form given Willie Mullins took it as he searched for the title and the selection looks well treated off an unchanged mark. This long straight will help and he can talk the pace likely set by the in form Fingal's Hill. The most interesting rival is bottom weight Arclight who is thrown in on his chase form and hinted at a revival last time where he suggested that this longer trip could be of benefit.

selections.comment: Those at the top of the weights appeal most here notably FANTASTIC LADY who has a good record in the Topham here and looked set to continue that until a race ending error at a key stage. She is well treated on her Listed form earlier in the season and should go close if her stamina holds up. Consistent veteran The Wolf is feared most as he was unsuited by a steady gallop last time so can do better here whilst Sail Away is also respected having proven his stamina recently. He ran well for a long way on ground softer than ideal last time but should find this more suitable.

selections.comment: Last year's winner Masked Dance is respected off 2lb higher having returned to form with a game runner up effort last time. However she may be vulnerable to top weight ILE DE JERSEY who hinted at a revival last time on her second start after a lay off. She has dropped to a very attractive mark based on her old form and the long straight should play to her strengths. The most interesting rival is Wudya who looks well treated for her stable debut with her latest runner up effort franked at Listed level this week. If her fitness holds up on her first start since the autumn she should be thereabouts.

He has run well at this venue in much stronger contests before so is respected despite top weight. However it is COME ON NIA who appeals most having run well in a hot Graded contest last time where she was given plenty to do. She was twice a winner last summer and looks dangerously well treated on her best novice form this term. She will need a decent pace but should get it from the likes of in form Fandabidozi who could hold on for a place.

selections.comment: NEWYORKSTATEOFMIND could well be the answer in a trappy handicap for the grade. The selection is a two-time C&D winner on good to firm, scoring off a mark of 66 last summer. The veteran runs off an 8lb lower mark here and the trainer and jockey combination boast an eyecatching 80 per cent strike-rate this season, with William Pyle winning on four of his five rides for trainer Ruth Carr. Refuge is respected, four of the veteran's seven wins have come over C&D, including on good to firm, and is 1lb below his last winning mark. Woohoo could hit the frame. More lightly raced than all bar one of her rivals, the four-year-old filly was denied a clear run last time out and can be rated higher than her bare form, that effort coming on her second start since switching yards from Ireland.

selections.comment: Dacres Cross sets the form standard for the runners with racecourse experience, finishing fifth of eight and fourth of eight in his first two starts, but may be vulnerable to a newcomer. The pick of those could be KOLKATA KNIGHT, an early foal with a speedy pedigree - dam ran in Listed class in Italy - the Tom Dascombe-trained colt makes the long trip up from Lambourn and is the yard's only runner on the card, and was sent here rather than Redcar on Monday. The yard are also 1/4 with their runners at the track over the last five years. Harlequin Bay is another interesting debutant. Speedily bred, he hails from a powerful yard that boast a 31% strike-rate at Hamilton with their two-year old runners over the last five years. The Charlie Johnston-trained Blue Mantle is bred to suit further than this but warrants a market check on debut

selections.comment: MAFTING was heavily backed over 10f on debut and although unable to convert that market confidence, the gelding was beaten just 3/4l, with the first two clear of the rest. The step up in trip should suit as his dam was a 12f Gr3 winner in France and two of his half-siblings were Group winners over 11f and 14f, and this step up in trip should suit his long-striding middle-distance action. The newcomer Me And Bobby McGee could give the selection most to do. Although more speedily bred than his four winning staying siblings, by the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint winner Bobby's Kitten, that colt won a Grade 3 over an extended 8f. The colt's dam won up to 14f and he is respected on debut from the powerful Charlie Johnston yard. Talismans Time may have been unsuited by soft ground when a well-held beaten favourite when last seen. Gelded since that run, he has possibilities breeding-wise stepped up in trip on quicker ground and the yard are in good form.

selections.comment: Creatif, rejuvenated by a wind op, could have more to come stepped up in trip and class. A winner on his penultimate start over 10.2f at Newcastle, the gelding showed his ability to act on the ground when second at Ripon last time out. Stamina should not be an issue as underlined by his wining debut over 12f at Saint-Cloud last season. While FAYLAQ may not be in the first flush of youth, the veteran posted a rock-solid win over 13f at the track last-time out, has won over shorter, acts on the ground and the yard target this race. Whathappensinvegas can be frustratingly inconsistent but hinted at a return to form last time out on seasonal return and has a squeak on the form of last season's 11f win at the track.

The gelding proved his ability to act on the ground there and could be a possible late bloomer as a four-year-old. Rain would help Onemorenomore's prospects

The drop back to 1m shouldn't prove too much of an issue (he went close on career debut over a mile when showing a decent turn of foot in a very narrow defeat) and he can defy the penalty to land the top spot again. Noble Horizon should put up a stern challenge having shown good promise on debut at Kempton when popular in the market. The son of Kingman should come on a fair bit for that and can serve it up to the selection. The Gosden's colt improved considerably on his career bow when beaten just under five lengths at Southwell upped to a mile form 7f on the back of a layoff. Better is expected and he appeals a tad more than Showyoutheropes who has a similar profile going into this

The drop back to 1m shouldn't prove too much of an issue (he went close on career debut over a mile when showing a decent turn of foot in a very narrow defeat) and he can defy the penalty to land the top spot again. Noble Horizon should put up a stern challenge having shown good promise on debut at Kempton when popular in the market. The son of Kingman should come on a fair bit for that and can serve it up to the selection. Of the newcomers Favorite Memory looks best and this Frankel filly could play a part but twice-raced Wicked is preferred to fill the frame. The Gosden's colt improved considerably on his career bow when beaten just under five lengths at Southwell upped to a mile form 7f on the back of a layoff. Better is expected and he appeals a tad more than Showyoutheropes who has a similar profile going into this

She showed a level in three runs last year that makes a mark of 64 look pretty appealing

selections.comment: KNIGHTSWOOD holds the strongest claims and can land a sixth career win. Charlie Johnston's gelding scored off 82 in a class 2 handicap at Ripon on penultimate run over this trip and put up another fine effort when upped to 1m6f off 87 being beaten under two lengths. His last four wins have come at 1m4f and the drop back to it here is a positive. He can run off 85 today (due to go up 2lb again in future) and has won in small fields. He'll be tough to get the better of. Fouroneohfever is the biggest danger. He took a big step forward last time looking more like the force of last spring/summer when landing a hat-trick before a fine 4th of 19 in the King George V stakes at Royal Ascot. However, most of his best form has come at tight tracks (namely Chester and Wolverhampton) and this track might not play to his strengths. Even so George Boughey's gelding is entitled to go close. Speriamo needs to come on a fair bit for a modest pipe-opener two weeks ago but, now likely to strip fitter and with the slight ease back in grade a help, the mare is marginally preferred to Lavender Hill Mob, who had been highly tried in Listed and Group company on the Flat before trying his luck in a handicap again last time looking as if his current mark is a bit stiff

selections.comment: Royal Accord should prove popular and has pretty solid claims. The son of Aclaim can go close having won two of his last three runs in class 6 events but is taken on here meeting slightly better company. The one to take the eye is BOW STREET. This son of Bated Breath would have fair claims based on the pick of his all-weather  form but there's a strong suspicion that a return to turf can spark a much improved effort. Three of his five turf runs rate higher than any on the AW and while that came at the start of his career the one AW run in that period was significantly poorer. He can bounce back from a poor effort (some excuse as needed room when pace lifted and wasn't knocked about once chance had gone). He could be worth chancing in a tight affair. Midnight City, dangerous if rediscovering some verve and Forever My Prince, winner of a nursery handicap when last seen and capable of going well fresh based on his career debut, need considering. However, Camera Shy is fancied to hit the frame. A course and distance winner on career debut, he's been handed a chance by the assessor with a pound drop after a decent 4th in a big field at Windsor last time

Feel the need is interesting back here after winning last term along with former course winners Eligible and Quest For Fun. YAASER arrives on the back of an easy win at Ayr and placed here last term, the booking of William Buick peaks interest in a wide open contest.

Top weight Dartan was far from disgraced having gone off too quickly on his last hurdles run. He completes the list of dangers.

selections.comment: Last year's winner The Dasher Conway is just 2lb higher this term and has hinted at a revival with midfield efforts the last twice. Back on a sound surface he could bounce back but may be vulnerable to the unexposed MARV MICHAEL who was a winner over hurdles and fences in the autumn. He was well fancied for a hot novice handicap at Cheltenham when last seen but met trouble. He's been freshened up since and could make a winning return off a lenient mark. Bottom weight Miss Oreo ran well for a long way until her fitness gave way last time but has dropped to an attractive mark on her summer form. She completes the list of dangers.
